title: Tryouts and Detention
premise: Paloma Montrose has spent five years as Hollow Creek High's statistician, quietly logging the impossible numbers that prove the school board is laundering money through the athletic program. When her best friend Theo vanishes days before the championship game, leaving behind a janitor's keyring he shouldn't have had, Paloma and her estranged ex, Delia, follow the keys into the school's sealed sub-basement and find Theo's evidence cache — and proof he's alive but hiding. As the board's enforcer, Coach Rennick, closes in and the last game becomes a deadline, Paloma must choose between the careful anonymity that kept her safe and broadcasting the truth to ten thousand people at once. She streams the buried records during the final buzzer, the board falls, and she and Delia walk out of detention together, finally unafraid.
about_author: Ivo Thackeray is a former high school scorekeeper who spent a decade in small-town Ohio before writing full time. Their novels dissect the quiet tyrannies of institutions through the eyes of the kids who count everything.

chapters.title: The Numbers Don't Lie, But I Do
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. During a routine game, she notices a $40,000 discrepancy in equipment invoices she's memorized, then deliberately misfiles her own report for the fifth year running. Emotional beat: the exhaustion of complicity — she knows, and knowing has become its own cage.

chapters.title: Theo's Bad Idea Face
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Theo pulls her behind the bleachers, buzzing with a secret he almost tells, pressing a folded note into her hand that just says 'if I go quiet, count the keys.' Emotional beat: dread disguised as banter; the reader sees the warning she doesn't.

chapters.title: Empty Desk, Full Lockers
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Theo misses first period, then the day. Delia, still raw from her breakup with Paloma, notices his locker cleaned out overnight — someone with master access. Emotional beat: the cold pivot from annoyance to fear.

chapters.title: The Keyring in the Vending Machine
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Following Theo's note, she finds seven unlabeled keys taped inside the broken vending machine by the gym. Coach Rennick watches her take them. Emotional beat: the moment being careful stops working.

chapters.title: Rennick's Friendly Warning
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Rennick offers her a college recommendation in exchange for 'keeping the stats clean' and mentions her scholarship depends on discretion. Emotional beat: corruption wearing a helpful smile; the trap of gratitude.

chapters.title: Delia Breaks In (Badly)
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Delia uses her detention-duty pass to search the athletic office and finds a shredder still warm, full of invoice strips. Rennick nearly catches her. Emotional beat: reckless courage — the opposite of Paloma's five careful years.

chapters.title: Seven Keys, Seven Doors
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Paloma and Delia, forced together by worry, test the keys after hours: equipment cage, records room, trophy case — and one that fits a door behind the boiler that shouldn't exist. Emotional beat: old intimacy flickering under adrenaline.

chapters.title: What's Under the Gym
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The sub-basement: a second set of books, cash boxes, and a wall of Theo's printouts — he'd been building a case for months. Emotional beat: awe curdling into terror; Theo knew everything and told no one, just like her.

chapters.title: Detention as Cover
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Delia gets deliberately assigned Saturday detention to search Rennick's office, and finds a photo of Theo taken the night he vanished — timestamped inside the school. Emotional beat: fury sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Board's Quiet Meeting
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Posing as a stats runner, Paloma sits outside a closed board session and hears them discuss 'the Montrose girl' and moving funds before the championship. Emotional beat: the hunters know her name now.

chapters.title: A Text from a Dead Account
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Theo messages from a burner: 'Don't come for me. I'm finishing it.' Delia realizes he's hiding voluntarily, protecting the evidence by disappearing. Emotional beat: relief tangled with betrayal — he didn't trust them either.

chapters.title: Paloma's Confession
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma tells Delia everything: five years of cooked reports, the threats that started sophomore year, why she never told anyone, including her. Emotional beat: the love story's wound reopened — honesty arriving years too late but not too late to matter.

chapters.title: Rennick Finds the Boiler Door
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. The sub-basement has been disturbed; someone else has a key. They find a camera Rennick installed and realize he's been watching them since the vending machine. Emotional beat: the walls closing in; paranoia becomes fact.

chapters.title: The Scholarship Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Rennick presents Paloma's falsified reports to her, offers full immunity if she testifies that Theo acted alone, and implies her mother's job at the district is leverage too. Emotional beat: power showing its teeth; duty weaponized against love.

chapters.title: Delia's Plan Is Insane
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Delia proposes streaming the sub-basement evidence live during the championship's halftime show, when ten thousand phones will be pointed at the gym anyway. Emotional beat: reckless hope — the plan only works if Paloma, the careful one, breaks her own rules.

chapters.title: Theo in the Flesh
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Theo surfaces at Paloma's window: he's been in the sub-basement's old bomb shelter, documenting, waiting for the game to guarantee an audience. He asks Paloma to be the one who presses record — the statistician's testimony carries weight. Emotional beat: reunion, forgiveness, and the weight of being chosen.

chapters.title: Countdown to Tip-Off
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Final preparations: Delia rigs the AV booth, Theo caches backups, Paloma rehearses her statement while Rennick circulates with a new security badge and a suspicious calm. Emotional beat: dread braided with resolve; the last quiet hours.

chapters.title: Halftime
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The feed goes live. Paloma reads the numbers — invoices, dates, Rennick's signature — as the jumbotron hijacks and phones rise across the stands like a field of lit matches. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into voice; five years of silence spent in four minutes.

chapters.title: Rennick in the AV Booth
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Rennick corners Delia in the booth, cutting power, but the stream is already mirrored on forty devices. He grabs the keyring; she lets him — his fingerprints are the last piece of proof. Emotional beat: sacrifice as strategy; Delia takes the hit so the truth survives.

chapters.title: The Last Buzzer
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The game ends in chaos and cheers; state investigators, tipped by a school board member saving herself, enter the gym as the final horn sounds. Rennick is escorted out past his own players. Emotional beat: justice arriving not through courts first but through a crowd that refuses to look away.

chapters.title: Detention
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Delia serves two weeks of real detention for the AV booth; Paloma visits daily through the door's window, doing homework on the hallway floor. The board resigns; Theo comes home to his furious, weeping parents. Emotional beat: consequences accepted gladly; love choosing to wait.

chapters.title: Clean Books
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Spring: Paloma hands the new board an honest ledger, keeps the statistician job on her terms, and walks out with Delia as the final bell rings. Emotional beat: the cage opened from inside; a first unhidden kiss in a parking lot that used to feel like enemy territory.
